newsitem.title: UK: Not guilty verdicts in British soccer-fixing trial.
newsitem.headline: Not guilty verdicts in British soccer-fixing trial.

text.p: Footballers John Fashanu and Hans Segers were found not guilty on Thursday of plotting to rig the results of matches in England's Premier Soccer League.
Fellow player Bruce Grobbelaar was also cleared of one charge of match-fixing but the jury was still out on a second charge against him.

The jury foreman said they had not reached an agreement on the final count against Grobbelaar, in which he was accused of corruptly accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,200) to influence or attempt to influence the outcome of a match or matches.
So the judge sent them home for a fifth night to resume their deliberations on Friday morning.

"It's been a nightmare for two and a half years. But we got the verdict we deserved ... Today is just an unbelievable day and it has been very emotional," Segers told reporters after the jury reached its verdict.
"I would like to resume my career. I am ready to go," the former Wimbledon goalkeeper said.
Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim was also cleared of attempting to fix matches.
"Obviously I am absolutely delighted and indeed hugely relieved," he told a melee of reporters outside the court.

It was the second time the quartet had been on trial in the case. An earlier jury failed to reach a verdict in what has been among the most sensational cases in British sport. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
